doors.label: Tax cap
doors.sentence: "Zero base all budget items with a view to holding tax increases to cost of living increases." Named NO on the 7 May 2026 budget (7.28 overall / 9.34 residential). Her reason is process and spending, not Kim's "tax hike was simply not enough."

doors.label: Downtown order
doors.sentence: "I have been a strong supporter of more bylaw and police enforcement on our streets." No Public Order Team and no 6am–10pm bylaw hours. The bylaw sentence is scored on M33, not here.

doors.label: Housing
doors.sentence: "Review and amend housing bylaws to conform with the minimum housing dictates of the Province (e.g. the City's Missing Middle provides for 50% more units than the Provincial mandate)." Record: named NO, 26 Jan 2023.

doors.label: Written program
doors.sentence: Authorized 2026 campaign site with four named priorities, a plan-bullet list, a voting-record page and a current donate/volunteer ask. Written and current. No costed budget, no unit target, no implementation calendar. The $300M→$160M reserve sentence is a campaign claim, not a verified City figure.

cells.quote: Review and amend housing bylaws to conform with the minimum housing dictates of the Province (e.g. the City's Missing Middle provides for 50% more units than the Provincial mandate).
cells.why: Disagrees with M6 supply: the 2026 ask is to cut City housing bylaws down to the provincial floor. Record matches, not a miss: named NO with Coleman and Hammond, 26 Jan 2023. Context, same article, not a second mark: she tried to refer the motion and called it "a flawed concept." Context, same Plan page, not scored separately: "set housing targets more in line with current projected population increases."

cells.quote: We have the bylaws to ensure safe streets. We need to enforce them.
cells.why: Commits to enforcing existing bylaws. Comparable, not Same: daytime sheltering is not named. 18 Jul 2024 motion passed 8–1 with Kim the lone named NO; Gardiner is not named in that article. Do not invent a YES. No sourced miss, so no incumbent cap.

cells.what: drug-use buffer (City: list + bylaw/DPOT + VicPD/CDSA; not City seizure)
cells.quote: Increase bylaw and police presence in neighbourhoods to enforce bylaws and laws regarding open use of illegal drugs.
cells.why: Commits to open-use enforcement. Neither the buffer list nor child-focused geography is named. The Harbour closure motion is the SCS sentence already on row 23, not a second mark here.

cells.quote: Ensure that the “solution” to street disorder downtown is not shifting encampments to neighbourhood park areas.
cells.why: Commits to keeping encampments out of neighbourhood parks. No named-space protocol, no night-lighting programme, no removal sequence.

cells.what: tax glide path (capped on the residential rate)
cells.quote: Zero base all budget items with a view to holding tax increases to cost of living increases.
cells.why: Commits to a COLA cap on tax increases. Comparable to M66's residential-rate glide path, not Same (no year-path, no override rule). ZBB in this sentence is already scored from the homepage on row 41 and is not a second mark. Record is a hit, not a miss: named NO on 7 May 2026 with Kim and Hammond. Do not copy Kim's "the tax hike was simply not enough" onto her. Her named reason: "Gardiner called the entire process flawed" and "We are digging ourselves into a hole while deceiving the public with soothing words about making Victoria a wonderful place to live." Adopted bill is 7.28 overall / 9.34 residential / 4.78 business. Do not stamp campaign 9.24 or 13.43 as ACTW figures.

cells.quote: I will zero-base the budget and demand every dollar delivers measurable results for residents.
cells.why: Commits to zero-based budgeting. Comparable, not Same: all-items ZBB, not rotating 3–4 areas, no three-part test. "Measurable results" in the same sentence is not a dashboard and is not scored on M67. Record matches: at the 7 May 2026 vote she "called for zero-based budgeting lens." No sourced miss (she voted NO on the non-ZBB bill), so no cap.

trees, mode share, ecosystems, emergency preparedness
cells.quote: Review Urban Forest targets with the objective of increasing canopy cover beyond parks through enhanced tree plantings in neighbourhoods, on boulevards and on private property.
cells.why: Commits to a canopy-increase review via plantings. Comparable to the trees half of M59–M63, not Same (no 5,000-tree number, no 35% canopy, no emergency-preparedness position). Record matches, not a second mark: she moved the 3 Apr 2025 canopy motion; Saanich News 4 Apr 2025: "In a pitch from Coun. Marg Gardiner, staff will add five-year tree canopy (growth) targets in the draft OCP supporting a 40 per cent, city-wide 2050 tree canopy goal." Campaign table restates that hit. OCP adoption NO (with Hammond and Coleman) is a density vote, not a trees miss. No sourced miss, so no cap. FLAG: Close is the high reading of "review with the objective of."

cells.quote: Eliminate planned generous salary increases for City Councillors and the Mayor, limiting increases to cost of living.
cells.why: Commits to COLA-limited remuneration. No lobbyist registry, no FOI-fee position. Record matches: named opposed to the 1 Aug 2024 remuneration package with Hammond; on 13 Nov 2025 she moved to cap the mayor's salary to inflation, named YES in a 6–3 fail with Hammond and Coleman. Verbatim from that meeting: "We need to cut the budget and as council we need to lead by cutting the purse strings on ourselves." CPI-only is the motion, not a second quote. Cluster mark is Partial because two of three instruments are absent.

cells.what: neighbourhoods, language access, Local Area Plans
cells.quote: Re-introduce the IAP2 consultation process — involve people in decision-making rather than informing the public after decisions are made.
cells.why: Commits to IAP2 as the neighbourhood-consultation instrument. Comparable, not Same: not official-languages access and not two Local Area Plans per year. Context, same Plan, not scored separately: "Give residents a greater say in the densification of their neighbourhoods"; "Review and amend the Delegation Bylaw"; expand residents' right to be informed and to appeal. Campaign table "Only Councillor to vote against" the Delegation Bylaw is her claim; no independent press URL opened this pass. FLAG, not a roll-call. No sourced miss, so no cap.

cells.what: community surveys, turnout and ballot access
Saanich amalgamation (one line, not the whole topic)
cells.why: and called on council to insist that a binding question be put on the municipal ballot in 2030." Named NO, with Caradonna, Hammond and Thompson, on putting the non-binding question on the 2026 ballot, 5–4. Commits to a binding amalgamation vote. Comparable to M81, not Same (2030, not this ballot). The NO on the 2026 voter question is a sourced miss vs putting amalgamation to voters now, so the incumbent cap holds this cell below Close. Not Opposed: she is not against amalgamation; she wants a stronger later instrument. Do not treat Kim/Loughton YES as the only hit.
